title: Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 37](/bible/exodus/37)

**[Exodus 37:1-5](/bible/exodus/37#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/37#v1)</sup> And Bezaleel made the ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it:
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/37#v2)</sup> And he overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made a crown of gold to it round about.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/37#v3)</sup> And he cast for it four rings of gold, to be set by the four corners of it; even two rings upon the one side of it, and two rings upon the other side of it.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/37#v4)</sup> And he made staves of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/37#v5)</sup> And he put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.

- Bezaleel made the ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, which is forty five inches, and a cubit and a half, which is twenty seven inches, the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it.
- It was wood overlaid with pure gold within and without, with a crown of gold round about it, and four rings of gold cast for the four corners; the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold were put into the rings by the sides of the ark to bear the ark. The staves stick out from the sides; that is how the ark was carried, and the priesthood always carried it.

**[Exodus 37:6-9](/bible/exodus/37#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/37#v6)</sup> And he made the mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half was the length thereof, and one cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/37#v7)</sup> And he made two cherubims of gold, beaten out of one piece made he them, on the two ends of the mercy seat;
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/37#v8)</sup> One cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the other end on that side: out of the mercy seat made he the cherubims on the two ends thereof.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/37#v9)</sup> And the cherubims spread out their wings on high, and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another; even to the mercy seatward were the faces of the cherubims.

- He made the mercy seat of pure gold, and two cherubims of gold beaten out of one piece on the two ends of the mercy seat, one cherub on the end on this side and another cherub on the other end on that side; the cherubims spread out their wings on high and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another.
- The most holy place, where the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat sat, was the central focus of the entire tabernacle: there the Most High spoke to the high priest above the mercy seat, in the area where the wings of the cherubims faced each other; the tablets of the law were placed inside the ark.
- Annually the high priest would sprinkle blood on the mercy seat to atone for the sins of all the people. The purpose and desire of the Most High is to dwell among His people and to commune with them; the layout of the tabernacle, with the steps of sacrifice and cleansing, is designed to bring sinful mankind to a loving and holy God.

**[Exodus 37:10-16](/bible/exodus/37#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/37#v10)</sup> And he made the table of shittim wood: two cubits was the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof:
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/37#v11)</sup> And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made thereunto a crown of gold round about.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/37#v12)</sup> Also he made thereunto a border of an handbreadth round about; and made a crown of gold for the border thereof round about.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/37#v13)</sup> And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings upon the four corners that were in the four feet thereof.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/37#v14)</sup> Over against the border were the rings, the places for the staves to bear the table.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/37#v15)</sup> And he made the staves of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold, to bear the table.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/37#v16)</sup> And he made the vessels which were upon the table, his dishes, and his spoons, and his bowls, and his covers to cover withal, of pure gold.

- He made the table of shittim wood: two cubits was the length thereof, a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof; he overlaid it with pure gold, with a crown of gold round about and a border of an hand breadth, and cast four rings of gold for the four corners that were in the four feet thereof, the places for the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear the table.
- This is the table of shewbread: on it Aaron and his sons placed twelve loaves of bread made from fine flour, and these twelve loaves represented the twelve tribes of Israel, a continual reminder of the everlasting promises, the covenant between the Most High and the children of Israel, and a memorial of His provision of food; the bread was eaten by Aaron and his sons and replaced every week on the sabbath.
- He made the vessels which were upon the table, his dishes, his spoons, his bowls, and his covers, of pure gold.

**[Exodus 37:17-24](/bible/exodus/37#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/37#v17)</sup> And he made the candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work made he the candlestick; his shaft, and his branch, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, were of the same:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/37#v18)</sup> And six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/37#v19)</sup> Three bowls made after the fashion of almonds in one branch, a knop and a flower; and three bowls made like almonds in another branch, a knop and a flower: so throughout the six branches going out of the candlestick.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/exodus/37#v20)</sup> And in the candlestick were four bowls made like almonds, his knops, and his flowers:
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/37#v21)</sup> And a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches going out of it.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/exodus/37#v22)</sup> Their knops and their branches were of the same: all of it was one beaten work of pure gold.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/exodus/37#v23)</sup> And he made his seven lamps, and his snuffers, and his snuffdishes, of pure gold.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/exodus/37#v24)</sup> Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof.

- He made the candlestick of pure gold, which is the menorah, all of one beaten work: his shaft, his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers were of the same, with six branches going out of the sides thereof, three out of the one side and three out of the other, the bowls made after the fashion of almonds, and his seven lamps.
- The knops and the flowers are the designs wrought into the work; the almond shaped bowls at the top held the olive oil where the lamps continually burned, and the light could not go out.
- Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof: a talent is close to eighty pounds.

**[Exodus 37:25-29](/bible/exodus/37#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/exodus/37#v25)</sup> And he made the incense altar of shittim wood: the length of it was a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit; it was foursquare; and two cubits was the height of it; the horns thereof were of the same.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/exodus/37#v26)</sup> And he overlaid it with pure gold, both the top of it, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: also he made unto it a crown of gold round about.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/exodus/37#v27)</sup> And he made two rings of gold for it under the crown thereof, by the two corners of it, upon the two sides thereof, to be places for the staves to bear it withal.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/exodus/37#v28)</sup> And he made the staves of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/exodus/37#v29)</sup> And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary.

- He made the incense altar of shittim wood: the length of it a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit, foursquare, and two cubits the height of it, the horns thereof of the same. First it was made with wood, and then he overlaid it with pure gold, both the top of it, and the sides round about, and the horns, with a crown of gold round about, two rings of gold under the crown, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear it withal.
- He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary, one who compounded such mixtures. The Lord required that special incense, a special sweet mixture of spices to be used only for the tabernacle, be burned consistently on this altar; none other was to be burned on it, and it was a matter of life and death.
- Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and there went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. They were not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to do certain services, and you could not just take it upon yourself to do them.
- Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 10:1-2](/bible/leviticus/10#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/10#v1)</sup> And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/10#v2)</sup> And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.

    Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not, and fire from the LORD devoured them; only the appointed could burn the incense on this altar.
